STAGE: metric family selection.
GOAL: pick a hyperbolic SID-table metric that is not a re-expression of prefix count / collision rate / same-bucket ratio, and not one of the four already measured (voronoi margin -0.081, adj R2 +0.156, hsoftmax path -0.488, Q_H +0.634).
READ: the task brief only; no table or recall file is readable in this session (no shell, no write, no data path).
OBSERVED: the brief states the plain hyperbolic path likelihood is confounded with level-2 bucket count (-0.78) and rewards collapse (12/2/3-code tables top the list); bucket count is -0.065; same-bucket ratio weak. So any global likelihood or global pair statistic is suspect, and any metric must be null-corrected for bucket size.
REASONING: the missing object is a LOCAL, geometry-conditioned statistic: for each item, where does its nearest same-bucket item sit in the curved nearest-neighbour order, relative to what a size-matched random partition would give? This is a first-moment statistic per item, not a global pair ratio; it is 0 for both collapse and random, positive only for geometric alignment, negative for anti-alignment. It is distinct from Q_H (code-statistics prefix ranking) because it uses the frozen reference's Poincare geodesic order.
OPEN: write the exact formula, verify degenerate cases, state compute cost.
EVIDENCE: none beyond the brief; this is a design record.

STAGE: formula sanity check for the chosen metric (hyperbolic bucket reach lift, HBRL).
GOAL: confirm the scalar is bounded, parameter-free, null-matched, and cheap.
READ: derived algebra only.
OBSERVED: let N items, level-1 bucket size n_b, e=N/n_b the exact expected rank of the first same-bucket item under a size-matched random partition. Define r_i = 1 + #{j: d_H(i,j) < d_H(i, nearest same-bucket mate)}. Per-item lambda is piecewise normalised: (e-r)/(e-1) for r<=e, (e-r)/(N-e) for r>e, and 0 when n_b=1 or n_b=N. Then lambda in [-1,1]; lambda=1 if the bucket mate is the geodesic nearest neighbour; lambda=0 at chance; lambda<0 if mates are farther than chance. M=mean(lambda) in [-1,1]. Checks: one-bucket collapse -> e=1,r=1 -> 0; all singletons -> e=N,r=N -> 0; random partition -> E[r]=e -> 0; perfect coherent bucket -> 1; anti-aligned bucket -> near -1. No constant is tuned: only N, n_b, and the reference curvature enter.
REASONING: the size-matched null is exact and analytic, so the collapse confound that killed the path likelihood is removed at construction, not by a post-hoc correction. Rank order under Poincare distance is computed from the monotone arcosh argument 1+2||zi-zj||^2/((1-||zi||^2)(1-||zj||^2)), so no arctanh is needed for ranking.
OPEN: compute cost is O(N^2 d) chunked; must state clipping near the ball boundary and tie-breaking.
EVIDENCE: algebra above; no data run.

STAGE: metric family selection and formula check (combined).
GOAL: choose a hyperbolic SID-table metric distinct from Q_H (+0.634), voronoi margin (-0.081), adj R2 (+0.156), hsoftmax path (-0.488), bucket count (-0.065) and same-bucket ratio, then verify degeneracies.
READ: task brief only; no table or recall file is readable in this session.
OBSERVED: the brief says path likelihood is confounded with level-2 bucket count (-0.78) and rewards collapse (12/2/3-code tables top). So global likelihoods and global pair ratios are suspect; the metric needs a per-item size-matched null.
REASONING: use a local curved-neighbourhood statistic. For each item, find the rank r_i of its nearest same-bucket item in the Poincare geodesic order, and compare to e_i=N/n_b, the exact expected rank under a size-matched random partition. Per-item lambda is piecewise normalised to [-1,1]: (e-r)/(e-1) for r<=e, (e-r)/(N-e) for r>e, 0 when n_b=N. M=mean(lambda). Checks: collapse one bucket -> 0; all singletons -> 0; random -> E[r]=e -> 0; perfect coherent bucket -> 1; anti-aligned -> near -1. Only N, n_b and the reference curvature enter; nothing is tuned. Rank order needs only the monotone arcosh argument, so O(N^2 d + N^2) chunked, well under a minute.
OPEN: empirical Spearman on the 97 pairs unknown; main risk is a noisy frozen reference or one built from the same clusters.
EVIDENCE: algebra above; no data run.

STAGE: final answer (complete block).
METRIC: hyp_bucket_reach_lift_l1
TITLE: Level-1 SID bucket reach lift under the reference Poincare metric.
FORMULA: N items; b(i)=level-1 code; n_b=|{j:b(j)=b(i)}|; z_i=frozen reference target representation, isometrically rescaled to the unit Poincare ball (curvature -1), ||z||^2 clipped to 1-1e-6. d_H(i,j)=arcosh(1+2||z_i-z_j||^2/((1-||z_i||^2)(1-||z_j||^2))). D_i=min_{j!=i,b(j)=b(i)} d_H(i,j). r_i=1+#{j!=i:(d_H(i,j),j)<(D_i,j_i*)}, j_i* the smallest index attaining D_i (tie-break by index); r_i is the 1-based rank of the nearest same-bucket item, r_i=1 when a bucket mate is the geodesic nearest neighbour. If n_b=1, r_i=N. Null rank e_i=N/n_b (expected rank of the first of n_b-1 mates placed uniformly among N-1 others). Per item: lambda_i=0 if n_b=1 or n_b=N; lambda_i=(e_i-r_i)/(e_i-1) if r_i<=e_i; lambda_i=(e_i-r_i)/(N-e_i) if r_i>e_i. M=(1/N)sum_i lambda_i, in [-1,1]. M=1 perfect geometric alignment, 0 chance, <0 anti-aligned.
INPUTS: exported Stage-2 SID table (level-1 integer code per item) and frozen Issue #126 reference target representation per item (training-pairs only; Poincare coords, or Euclidean mapped by exp_0 at the reference's fixed curvature). Nothing else.
GEOMETRY: Poincare ball, curvature -1 after the isometry x->sqrt(c_ref)x (order-preserving, untuned). The curved metric enters in every r_i: the nearest same-bucket item is found by expanding a hyperbolic ball, and hyperbolic NN != Euclidean NN, so the rank order exists only through d_H. The null e_i is rank-based, so only the observed rank carries geometry.
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL: Stage 3 reranks the level-1 bucket Stage 2 selects, so Recall@10 needs the bucket of target i to be a coherent curved neighbourhood of i: a query near i then lands in a bucket of i's geodesic neighbours and i survives reranking. HBRL measures this locally and contrasts it with the exact size-matched random partition, so bucket size and collapse cannot drive it. Over Q_H (+0.634, code-statistics prefix ranking) it adds the orthogonal test of whether the partition follows the reference's curved geometry. Unlike the path likelihood (-0.49, confounded with bucket count at -0.78, top values on 12/2/3-code collapsed tables) the analytic null makes collapse and random both 0, and only alignment positive. It is not bucket count or same-bucket ratio: those are global pair statistics high for collapse and for fine random tables alike, while HBRL is a per-item first-moment statistic that is 0 in both cases.
COMPUTE: N=24587, 256 codes. Build the N x N arcosh argument in row chunks (512 rows, ~50 MB float32); rank by the monotone argument without arcosh; per row take the same-bucket min and count closer items. O(N^2 d + N^2), ~6e8 entries, seconds to well under a minute on CPU for d<=256. No iteration, no optimisation.
RISKS: noisy frozen reference -> all M near 0 and no Spearman; reference built from the same clustering -> M saturates and loses variance; boundary points need the clip; duplicate representations need the index tie-break; singleton-dominated tables contribute 0; if Recall@10 is driven by Stage-2 token generation rather than Stage-3 candidate geometry the signal is weak.
FAILURE MODE: worst on the anti-aligned table that orders items along a hyperbolic diameter and interleaves the two ends into level-1 buckets, so each bucket holds geometrically opposite items: r_i>>e_i, lambda_i -> -1, M -> -1. Random-hash codes and the one-bucket collapse both give M=0 (neutral, never rewarded), so the anti-aligned partition is the true worst case.
END METRIC
